mainTopic: Forbidden phrasings in public prayer, the reasons the prayer leader is silenced, and which sensitive passages are read, translated, or used as a הפטרה
overview: This amud finishes a משנה about phrases a שליח ציבור may not say and improper ways of reading or translating the Torah in public. The גמרא explains why מודים מודים and על טוב יזכר שמך are a problem. Two אמוראים then dispute why על קן צפור יגיעו רחמיך is forbidden: it causes jealousy among the creations, or it turns ה׳'s decrees into mercy. Two stories follow. In the first, רבה praises a prayer leader only to sharpen אביי. In the second, רבי חנינא rebukes a man who added extra praises of ה׳. רבי חנינא also teaches that everything is in Heaven's hands except יראת שמים. רבי זירא compares repeating שמע to מודים מודים, and the גמרא distinguishes repeating word by word from repeating verse by verse. The גמרא explains the עריות and מולך clauses of the משנה. A new משנה then lists passages that are read but not translated, and passages not used as a הפטרה. Its ברייתא begins with מעשה בראשית, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Saying 'May the good bless You' is a path of heresy
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a שליח ציבור who says יברכוך טובים is following the way of מינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'May the good people bless You,' this is the way of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches that one specific prayer phrase is a sign of heresy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase suggests that only good people bless ה׳. That fits a heretical view that splits the world into two domains, good and evil, each with its own power. Real belief is that everyone, good and bad, stands under ה׳ alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Heresy, especially dualistic belief in more than one power

phrases.english: "May the good bless You"
phrases.notes: Part of the משנה's list of improper phrases in prayer

phrases.english: this is a path of heresy.
phrases.notes: It sounds like only the good belong to ה׳, as if there were two powers, one for good and one for bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְבָרְכוּךָ טוֹבִים הֲרֵי זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הַמִּינוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of improper prayer phrases from the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying יברכוך טובים in prayer is a path of מינות.

steps.title: Three prayer phrases that get the prayer leader silenced
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three phrases that get a שליח ציבור silenced: על קן צפור יגיעו רחמיך, על טוב יזכר שמך, and מודים מודים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'Your mercy reaches even a bird's nest,' or 'May Your name be mentioned for the good,' or 'We thank, we thank,' they silence him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three more phrases. Anyone who says them in public prayer is stopped right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not give reasons here. It only gives the ruling: משתקין אותו, meaning they stop him from going on. The גמרא will soon explain each of the three.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird's nest; refers to the מצוה of sending away the mother bird
They silence him; he is stopped from leading

phrases.english: "Your mercy extends to a bird's nest,"
phrases.notes: Meaning: just as You pity the mother bird, pity us too

phrases.english: and "May Your name be mentioned for the good,"
"We give thanks, we give thanks"
phrases.notes: Saying the word twice

phrases.english: they silence him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds three more forbidden prayer phrases to the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח ציבור who says על קן צפור יגיעו רחמיך, על טוב יזכר שמך, or מודים מודים is silenced.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three cases are exactly what the גמרא analyzes below.

steps.title: Using euphemisms when reading the forbidden relations section
steps.stepSummary: Someone who softens the wording when reading the פרשת עריות in public is silenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone reading the Torah changes the words of the forbidden relations section into gentler language, they silence him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from prayer to public Torah reading. Changing the text of עריות, even out of modesty, is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the words is wrong even when the motive is a sense of propriety. The Torah must be read exactly as written. So the reader is stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: One who uses a substitute name or euphemism
Forbidden sexual relations; the Torah section listing them

phrases.english: One who uses euphemisms in the section of forbidden relations
phrases.notes: For example, changing 'the nakedness of your father' to 'the shame of your father'

phrases.english: they silence him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from forbidden prayer phrases to improper Torah reading
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who uses euphemisms when reading the עריות section is silenced.

steps.title: A false translation of the Molech verse is silenced with rebuke
steps.stepSummary: Someone who translates the מולך verse as a ban on having children with an Aramean woman is silenced with a sharp rebuke.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone translates 'Do not give your children to pass over to Molech' as 'Do not give your seed to impregnate an Aramean woman,' they silence him and rebuke him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case of mistranslating a verse during the public reading. This case is treated more harshly, with silencing plus a rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The translator turns a verse about idolatry into a verse about relations with gentiles. This twists the plain meaning of the Torah, so he gets a rebuke (נזיפה) and not just silencing. His wordplay hangs on להעביר (pass over) and לאעברא (impregnate).

keyTerms.meaning: An idolatrous practice of passing children through fire

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two silencing rulings. In the עריות case he is just silenced. Here he is silenced בנזיפה, with an added rebuke, because he changed the verse's meaning entirely.

phrases.english: One who says:
"'And you shall not give any of your seed to pass over to Molech' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:21

phrases.english: you shall not give it to impregnate an Aramean woman"
phrases.notes: His false Aramaic translation

phrases.english: they silence him with a rebuke.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר וּמִזַּרְעֲךָ לֹא תִתֵּן לְהַעֲבִיר לַמּוֹלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another improper public reading, here a translation, with a harsher response
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who mistranslates the מולך verse as referring to an Aramean woman is silenced with a rebuke.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three levels: מינות (יברכוך טובים), silencing (the three phrases and עריות euphemisms), and silencing with נזיפה (the מולך mistranslation).

steps.title: Two reasons are clear, but why is the bird's nest phrase forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why מודים מודים and על טוב יזכר שמך are problems. It then asks what is wrong with על קן צפור יגיעו רחמיך.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense why 'We thank, we thank' is silenced, since it looks like praying to two powers. 'May Your name be mentioned for the good' also makes sense. It implies thanks only for good and not for bad, yet we learned that a person must bless ה׳ for bad just as for good. But 'Your mercy reaches a bird's nest': what is wrong with that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the reasons for two of the משנה's three cases. It then sets up its real question about the third case, the bird's nest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מודים מודים sounds like thanking two separate powers. על טוב יזכר שמך limits praise to good events, which goes against the משנה in ברכות that we bless for bad too. על קן צפור sounds like a sweet praise of ה׳'s mercy, so its problem is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (sets up a contrast with a harder case)

steps.confusionAlert: The בשלמא part is not the question. It only clears away the easy cases. The real question comes after the word אלא.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Granted, "We give thanks, we give thanks"
since it looks like two authorities.
"May Your name be mentioned for the good" also makes sense,
since it implies: for the good, yes,
but for the bad, no,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה
phrases.english: and we learned: A person is obligated to bless for the bad
phrases.notes: משנה ברכות 54a

phrases.english: just as he blesses for the good.
But "Your mercy extends to a bird's nest":
what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts analyzing the three phrases from step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is a שליח ציבור silenced for saying על קן צפור יגיעו רחמיך?

steps.title: First answer: it causes jealousy among creations
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל, רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא, disagree. One says the phrase stirs up jealousy among ה׳'s creations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two אמוראים in the West, רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא, disagree about this. One said: because he casts jealousy into the works of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by bringing a dispute. This step gives the first of the two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying ה׳'s mercy reaches the bird, the speaker implies that ה׳ favors the bird over other creatures. That makes it look as if ה׳ plays favorites, which causes jealousy among His creations.

keyTerms.meaning: The works of creation, all created beings

phrases.english: Two Amoraim in the West disagree about it:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida.
One said:
because he casts jealousy among the works of creation,
phrases.notes: As if ה׳ favored the bird over other creatures

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase implies that ה׳ favors one creature, which causes jealousy among His creations.

steps.title: Second answer: ה׳'s commandments are decrees, not mercy
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says the phrase is wrong because it treats ה׳'s מצוות as acts of mercy, when they are really royal decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: because he makes the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He, into mercy, when they are nothing but decrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second opinion. It explains the problem with על קן צפור in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the מצוה of שילוח הקן comes from mercy claims to know the reason behind the מצוה. This view holds that מצוות are גזירות, decrees of the King that we keep whether or not we know why. Calling them mercy turns a command into a feeling.

keyTerms.meaning: His attributes, here meaning His commandments
The Holy One, Blessed be He
Decrees of the King, to be kept without knowing the reason

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for silencing על קן צפור. One: it causes jealousy among creations. Two: it presents מצוות as mercy when they are גזירות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The second view is a famous source for the idea that we keep מצוות as ה׳'s decrees, not only because we understand their reasons.

phrases.english: And one said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רַחֲמִים,
phrases.english: because he makes the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He, into mercy,
and they are nothing but decrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רַחֲמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the dispute, a different reason from step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase treats ה׳'s מצוות as acts of mercy, when they are really decrees.

steps.title: A prayer leader before רבה asks for mercy based on קן צפור, and רבה praises him
steps.stepSummary: A שליח ציבור prays: 'You had pity on the bird's nest and on אותו ואת בנו, so have pity on us.' רבה seems to praise him for knowing how to win ה׳'s favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man went down to lead the prayers in front of רבה. He said: 'You had pity on the bird's nest, so have pity and mercy on us! (You had pity on a mother animal and its young, so have pity and mercy on us.)' רבה said: 'How well this scholar knows how to win over his Master!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. A prayer leader uses exactly the kind of קן צפור phrase our משנה says to silence, and רבה seems to approve of it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view in step 7 held that מצוות like קן צפור and אותו ואת בנו are royal decrees, not acts of mercy. This prayer leader treats them as mercy and builds his request on that idea. Whatever the reason, the משנה says to silence such a phrase, so רבה's praise looks like it goes against the משנה, and a challenge is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before (the ark), meaning he led the prayers
The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day
To win the favor of his Master (ה׳)

phrases.english: A certain man who went down (to lead prayers) before Rabba said:
You had pity on the bird's nest —
have pity and mercy on us!
(You had pity on 'it and its young' —
phrases.notes: Refers to the ban on slaughtering an animal and its offspring on one day.

phrases.english: have pity and mercy on us.)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַבָּה: כַּמָּה יָדַע הַאי מֵרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: Rabba said: How much this scholar knows
how to win over his Master!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case of the קן צפור phrase that steps 5-7 explained is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה seemingly praises a prayer leader who used the קן צפור plea.

steps.title: אביי objects: the משנה says to silence him
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: our משנה rules that someone who says this is silenced, so how can you praise him?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: 'But we learned in the משנה, "They silence him"!'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, רבה's student, challenges his teacher's praise by quoting our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says to silence anyone who says 'על קן צפור יגיעו רחמיך'. This prayer leader said the same idea, so he should have been silenced, not praised. The challenge is direct: רבה's reaction seems to go against an explicit משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But we learned (in the mishna): 'They silence him'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's praise in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's praise of the prayer leader
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says to silence anyone who says the קן צפור phrase, so praising him goes against the משנה.

steps.title: רבה was only testing אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבה really agreed with the משנה. He only praised the prayer leader to sharpen אביי's mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה (did not really mean it); he only wanted to sharpen אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge by explaining what רבה was really doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה did not disagree with the משנה. He made a surprising comment on purpose to see whether אביי would notice the problem and quote the משנה. So the rule stands: this phrase is not allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה argues with the משנה. His praise was a teaching test, not his real opinion.

phrases.english: And Rabba — he only wanted to sharpen Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה really approved of the קן צפור plea, against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה agreed with the משנה and only spoke this way to test and sharpen אביי.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule stands: a prayer leader who builds his plea on קן צפור as an act of mercy is silenced. רבה's praise was only a test for אביי.

steps.title: A prayer leader before רבי חנינא adds extra praises of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: Someone leading prayers before רבי חנינא added three more praises to the standard 'הגדול הגבור והנורא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man went down to lead the prayers in front of רבי חנינא. He said: 'The God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome, the powerful, the strong, and the fearless.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story about adding words to prayer. This sets up רבי חנינא's rebuke in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The standard ברכה of אבות says only three praises: הגדול, הגבור, והנורא. This prayer leader added three more of his own (האדיר, והחזק, והאמיץ). The question is whether adding more praise is a good thing.

keyTerms.meaning: The great, the mighty, and the awesome (the standard three praises)
The powerful, the strong, the fearless (his added praises)

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אָמַר:
phrases.english: A certain man who went down (to lead prayers) before Rabbi Ḥanina said:
'The God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome,
the powerful, and the strong, and the fearless.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, also about a prayer leader who adds words of his own to prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A prayer leader adds extra praises beyond the standard three.

steps.title: רבי חנינא rebukes him: even the three praises need special permission
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא sarcastically asks if he has finished all of ה׳'s praises. He explains that we only say the three standard praises because משה wrote them in the תורה and the כנסת הגדולה put them into תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said to him: 'Have you finished all the praises of your Master? Even these three praises, if משה had not written them in the תורה and the כנסת הגדולה had not come and set them into the prayer, we would not say them. And you said all of this!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא rebukes the prayer leader and explains why adding praises is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rebuke is a sarcastic question: by listing praises, you act as if ה׳'s praises could ever be finished. Even the three standard praises are only allowed because the תורה and the כנסת הגדולה gave us permission. Adding more on your own goes beyond what we are permitted to say.

keyTerms.meaning: The Men of the Great Assembly, who set the text of תפילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why we do not add our own praises to the fixed wording of the ברכות. We stick to the text set by the תורה and the חכמים.

phrases.english: He said to him: Have you finished all the praises of your Master?
Now, these three (praises),
if Moses had not written them in the Torah,
phrases.notes: דברים 10:17

phrases.english: and the Great Assembly had not come and set them (into the prayer) —
we would not say them.
And you said all of this!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the added praises in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not add praises of ה׳ beyond the three set by משה and the כנסת הגדולה.

steps.title: The parable: praising a billionaire for his silver coins
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא gives a parable. Praising a man who owns countless gold coins for owning a thousand silver coins is an insult, not a compliment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a man who had thousands upon thousands of gold coins, and people praised him for having a thousand silver coins. Isn't that an insult to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא backs up his rebuke with a parable that shows why extra praise actually takes away from ה׳'s honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳'s true greatness is endless, like piles of gold. Any list of praises we can make is tiny next to that, like a few silver coins. A longer list does not add honor. It only makes it look as if we think our small list describes Him.
steps.whatToRemember: We say only the three praises the תורה and the כנסת הגדולה gave us. Adding our own praises is not more honor, because any human praise is tiny compared to ה׳'s real greatness.

phrases.english: A parable: to a man who had
thousands upon thousands of gold dinars,
and people praised him for (a thousand) silver dinars.
Isn't that an insult to him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי חנינא's rebuke in step 12 with a parable.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should not add extra praises of ה׳
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parable of praising a very rich man for a small amount of silver

steps.title: Everything is in Heaven's hands except fear of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא teaches that השם controls everything except whether a person fears Him, and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except for fear of Heaven, as it says: 'And now, Israel, what does ה׳ your God ask of you other than to fear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another, separate teaching from רבי חנינא, who was just mentioned in the previous steps. He says a person's fear of Heaven is the one thing left to the person's own choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: השם decides almost everything about a person's life, but not whether he will fear Heaven. The proof is that the פסוק describes השם as asking us to fear Him. You only ask someone for something that is in his power to give.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything is in the hands of Heaven
As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for בחירה (free will): fear of Heaven is a person's own responsibility.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Everything is in the hands of Heaven
except for fear of Heaven,
as it is stated:
"And now, Israel,
what does the Lord your God ask of you
phrases.notes: דברים 10:12

phrases.english: other than to fear."
phrases.notes: Since ה׳ 'asks' for it, it must be up to us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching from the same רבי חנינא quoted in steps 11-13, brought because his name came up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything is decided by Heaven except a person's fear of Heaven, which is his own choice.

steps.title: Is fear of Heaven really a small thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of the פסוק: 'what does ה׳ ask of you other than to fear' makes יראה sound like a small request.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that fear of Heaven is a small matter?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the פסוק is worded. The phrase 'only to fear' sounds like יראה is an easy, minor request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'all He asks is just X' suggests X is small. But fear of Heaven is huge and hard to reach. So how could the פסוק talk about it as if it were simple?

phrases.english: By inference, that fear
is a small matter?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק 'מה ה׳ אלהיך שואל מעמך כי אם ליראה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'only' implies a small request, but יראת שמים is clearly a great and difficult thing.

steps.title: For משה רבינו it was a small matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that yes, for משה רבינו, who was speaking, fear of Heaven really was a small thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, for משה our teacher it is a small matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The words were said by משה, and for him יראה really was small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is speaking from the point of view of the speaker, משה רבינו. He had fully reached יראת שמים, so to him it felt simple. It is not saying יראה is objectively easy for everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying fear of Heaven is unimportant. It is saying it felt small only to משה, because he already had so much of it.

phrases.english: Yes,
for Moses our teacher
it is a small matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees with the inference but limits it to the speaker's own level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say יראה is small for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was small only from משה רבינו's point of view.

steps.title: Parable of the large and small vessel
steps.stepSummary: A parable shows why something you already own feels small, and something you lack feels big.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a person who is asked for a large vessel: if he has it, it seems to him like a small vessel. If he is asked for a small one and does not have it, it seems to him like a large vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a parable. Whether a request feels big or small depends on whether you already have the thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you own a big item, being asked for it feels easy. If you don't own even a small item, being asked for it feels hard. משה owned great יראה, so asking for it felt small to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable; it is comparable to

steps.whatToRemember: Fear of Heaven is up to each person. The פסוק calls it 'only' because to משה, who had plenty of it, it felt small.

phrases.english: It is comparable to a person
from whom they request a large vessel
and he has it —
it seems to him like a small vessel.
A small one, and he does not have it —
it seems to him like a large vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁמְּבַקְּשִׁין הֵימֶנּוּ כְּלִי גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the answer of step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That יראה could seem small to משה רבינו
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parable about asking for large and small vessels

steps.title: Saying 'שמע שמע' is like saying 'מודים מודים'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rules that repeating שמע is like repeating מודים, which our משנה says gets a person silenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: One who says 'שמע, שמע' is like one who says 'מודים, מודים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of the משנה about silencing a prayer leader. רבי זירא adds that repeating שמע is just as bad as repeating מודים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one who says 'מודים מודים' is silenced, because it sounds like he is thanking two different powers. רבי זירא extends this: repeating שמע also sounds like accepting two different powers. So he too should be silenced.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
One who says "Shema, Shema" —
is like one who says "Modim, Modim."
phrases.notes: The משנה rules that such a person is silenced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side teaching of רבי חנינא to the משנה's rule about silencing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating שמע is treated like repeating מודים, so the person is silenced.

steps.title: A ברייתא says repeating שמע is only disgraceful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא from a ברייתא that calls repeating שמע 'disgraceful', which implies he is not silenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who reads שמע and repeats it, this is disgraceful. It is disgraceful, but we do not silence him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא with a ברייתא. The ברייתא only calls repeating שמע 'disgraceful', not something you silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If repeating שמע were like repeating מודים, the ברייתא should say 'we silence him'. Saying only 'disgraceful' implies a lighter level. So the ברייתא seems to contradict רבי זירא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who recites Shema and repeats it —
this is disgraceful.
It is disgraceful,
but we do not silence him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's ruling in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's ruling that repeating שמע gets one silenced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא only calls it 'disgraceful', which implies it is not serious enough to silence him.

steps.title: Word by word versus verse by verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא and רבי זירא talk about two different kinds of repeating.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this case is where he says each word and repeats it; that case is where he says each verse and repeats it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases. One source talks about repeating single words, the other about repeating whole פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating word by word just ruins the reading, so it is only 'disgraceful', like the ברייתא says. Repeating a whole פסוק sounds like accepting two powers, so the person is silenced, like רבי זירא says. Both sources are correct, each in its own case.
steps.confusionAlert: Many beginners assume repeating one word is worse. It is the opposite here: repeating a whole פסוק is worse and gets you silenced, because it sounds like two separate acceptances.
steps.whatToRemember: Repeating שמע word by word is disgraceful but you are not silenced. Repeating a whole פסוק is like 'מודים מודים' and you are silenced.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר מִילְּתָא מִילְּתָא וְתָנֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: this is where he says each word and repeats it,
phrases.notes: This is the case the ברייתא calls disgraceful, but he isn't silenced.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר פְּסוּקָא פְּסוּקָא וְתָנֵי לֵהּ.
phrases.english: that is where he says each verse and repeats it.
phrases.notes: This is the case where he is silenced, as רבי זירא said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by separating two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רבי זירא seemed to disagree about whether one who repeats שמע is silenced.
steps.terutzMaskana: Repeating word by word is only disgraceful. Repeating a whole פסוק gets one silenced.

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe he repeated שמע because he lost focus
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רבא why repeating שמע should be considered improper. Perhaps he did not concentrate the first time and is now saying it properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But maybe the first time he did not focus his mind, and now he is focusing his mind?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the ruling that repeating שמע is improper. He offers an innocent reason for the repetition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 19 called repeating שמע מגונה (disgraceful), and step 20 applied that to repeating word by word. רב פפא suggests a harmless explanation: he lacked כוונה the first time and is repeating to fix it. If so, why call the repetition disgraceful at all? (This is one reading; the question can also be read as challenging the silencing of one who repeats a whole פסוק.)

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe / perhaps (introduces an alternative possibility)
He focused his mind (had proper concentration, כוונה)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But perhaps at first he did not focus his mind,
and now he is focusing his mind?
phrases.notes: So the repetition would be innocent. Why then call it disgraceful?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling (steps 19-20) that repeating שמע is disgraceful.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that one who repeats שמע is מגונה (disgraceful).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repeating might come from a sincere wish to say it again with כוונה. If so, it seems wrong to call the repetition disgraceful.

steps.title: רבא: you may not treat Heaven so casually
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a person may not act so casually with Heaven. Someone who fails to concentrate should be forced to concentrate, not allowed to repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is one allowed to be 'buddies' with Heaven? If he does not focus his mind, we beat him with a blacksmith's hammer until he focuses his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב פפא's excuse. Saying words to Heaven carelessly and then redoing them is itself unacceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny that the person may have lacked focus. He says that is no excuse. Treating prayer like a casual chat you can redo is too familiar with Heaven, so the repetition is rightly called disgraceful. The hammer is strong language that stresses how serious this is.

keyTerms.meaning: I strike him / we beat him

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not giving a real legal punishment of beating. The 'blacksmith's hammer' is vivid language for how unacceptable careless prayer is.
steps.whatToRemember: Repeating a whole פסוק of שמע gets one silenced, and repeating word by word is disgraceful. 'I wasn't concentrating the first time' is not an accepted excuse, because one may not act casually toward Heaven.

phrases.english: He said to him: Can one be 'buddies' with Heaven?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course not.

phrases.english: If he does not focus his mind,
we beat him with a blacksmith's hammer
until he focuses his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the excuse: lack of focus does not permit repeating; it calls for forcing focus.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating to fix missing כוונה should not be considered disgraceful.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying words to Heaven carelessly and then redoing them is too casual toward Heaven, so the repetition is rightly called disgraceful. He should have concentrated the first time.

steps.title: What 'softening' the עריות passage means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about one who 'softens' the עריות. רב יוסף explains it as saying 'the shame of his father and mother' instead of 'the nakedness of your father and mother'.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] One who changes the wording in the עריות passage is silenced. רב יוסף taught: this means one who says 'the shame of his father and the shame of his mother'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the earlier משנה. It explains what kind of wording change the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'ערות אביך וערות אמך'. The reader changes it to the softer 'קלון' (shame) and turns it into third person. Rewording the Torah's text this way, even to make it politer, is not allowed, so he is silenced.

keyTerms.meaning: One who uses a substitute or euphemistic wording

phrases.english: One who uses substitute wording for the forbidden relations is silenced.
phrases.notes: A quotation from the משנה being explained.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
[One who says] 'the shame of his father and the shame of his mother'.
phrases.notes: Instead of 'the nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother' (ויקרא 18:7).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמע discussion and explains a different clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Changing 'ערות' to 'קלון' in the עריות passage is the 'softening' the משנה forbids; the reader is silenced.

steps.title: The מולך verse: which reading gets silenced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of translating 'ומזרעך לא תתן להעביר למלך' in a strange way. It cites the school of רבי ישמעאל, who read the verse as being about a Jew who fathers a child with a non-Jewish woman, and the child is raised for idolatry.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] One who says [in translating] 'And you shall not give of your seed to pass over', etc. [is silenced with a rebuke]. The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: the verse is speaking about a Jew who has relations with a non-Jewish woman and fathers from her a son for idolatry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last clause of the earlier משנה. It shows where the odd translation of the מולך verse comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The translator reads 'giving your seed' as fathering children with a non-Jew. This follows the school of רבי ישמעאל, who saw such a child as raised for idolatry. The משנה silences the translator because he presents this reading in public in place of the verse's plain meaning about giving children to מולך.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: The reader or translator may not reword or reinterpret the Torah in public. That covers the 'softening' of עריות and the non-literal translation of the מולך verse.

phrases.english: One who says: 'And you shall not give of your seed to pass over', etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה (ויקרא 18:21): this is someone who twists the פסוק into having children with an Aramean woman.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
About a Jew who has relations with a non-Jewish woman
and fathers from her a son for idolatry
the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining clauses of the משנה, moving to the next case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The odd translation comes from reading the verse as being about fathering a child with a non-Jew who will be raised for idolatry. Translating it this way in public earns a rebuke.

steps.title: New משנה: passages read but not translated
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists sensitive passages. Some are read and translated in public: תמר and the first account of the עגל. Others are read but not translated: ראובן, the second account of the עגל, ברכת כהנים, and דוד and אמנון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The story of ראובן is read but not translated. The story of תמר is read and translated. The first account of the Golden Calf is read and translated; the second is read but not translated. ברכת כהנים and the story of דוד and אמנון are read but not translated.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us which embarrassing or sensitive Torah and נביא passages get the Aramaic translation in public and which do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every passage listed is still read in the original Hebrew. The only question is whether the תרגום is said aloud for the public, which could lead simple listeners to misunderstand or think less of great people. The גמרא that follows will explain each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Is translated (into Aramaic for the public)
The incident of the Golden Calf
The story of David's son Amnon (שמואל ב 13)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not translated' does NOT mean 'not read'. Every passage here is still read aloud in Hebrew; only the Aramaic translation is held back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle of public Torah reading: the text itself is never skipped, but its public explanation is managed with care for the honor of great people and the understanding of the listeners.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The incident of Reuben is read but not translated.
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:22, ראובן and בלהה.

phrases.english: The incident of Tamar is read and translated.
phrases.notes: בראשית 38.

phrases.english: The first account of the Calf is read and translated,
phrases.notes: The Torah's own telling of the event (שמות 32:1–20).

phrases.english: and the second is read but not translated.
phrases.notes: אהרן's report to משה (שמות 32:21–24).

phrases.english: The Priestly Blessing and the incident of David and Amnon —
are read but not translated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַעֲשֵׂה רְאוּבֵן נִקְרָא וְלֹא מִתַּרְגֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, related in theme (sensitive passages in public reading) but a separate unit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sensitive passages are always read. ראובן, the second account of the עגל, ברכת כהנים, and דוד and אמנון are not translated; תמר and the first account of the עגל are translated.

steps.title: No הפטרה from the מרכבה vision or from 'הודע את ירושלים'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by ruling that the מרכבה may not be used as a הפטרה, while רבי יהודה permits it. רבי אליעזר also forbids 'הודע את ירושלים' as a הפטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not read the Chariot vision as the הפטרה, and רבי יהודה permits it. רבי אליעזר says: we do not read 'Make known to Jerusalem' as the הפטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of sensitive passages with two rules about the הפטרה, the reading from the Prophets after the Torah reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מרכבה (יחזקאל 1) is a deep, hidden subject, so the תנא קמא does not want it publicized. רבי יהודה disagrees and allows it. רבי אליעזר adds a different kind of concern: 'הודע את ירושלים' (יחזקאל 16) harshly describes the sins of the Jewish people, so it should not be read publicly as a הפטרה.

keyTerms.meaning: conclude the Torah reading with a reading from the Prophets (the הפטרה)
the Divine Chariot vision in Ezekiel chapter 1
'Make known to Jerusalem [her abominations]', Ezekiel 16, a harsh rebuke

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different reasons here. The מרכבה is avoided because it is too holy and hidden. 'הודע את ירושלים' is avoided because it is embarrassing to the Jewish people. Do not merge them into one reason.

phrases.english: We do not conclude with the Chariot vision as the haftarah,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל chapter 1

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda permits it.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
We do not conclude with 'Make known to Jerusalem.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַפְטִירִין בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of sensitive passages, now moving from Torah readings to הפטרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מרכבה is not read as a הפטרה (רבי יהודה permits it). According to רבי אליעזר, 'הודע את ירושלים' is not read as a הפטרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא sorts passages into three groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. Some passages are read and translated, some are read but not translated, and some are neither read nor translated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: some passages are read and translated, some are read but not translated, and some are neither read nor translated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that gives a three-way framework for the whole topic. This sets up the detailed lists that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed cases one by one. The ברייתא organizes them into three clear groups, adding a group the משנה only hinted at: passages that are not read in public at all. The rest of the סוגיא will fill in each group.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
are translated into Aramaic for the congregation

steps.whyThisMatters: This three-part framework is the map for the rest of the סוגיא. Every passage discussed afterward fits into one of these three groups.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught:
There are passages that are read and translated,
and there are passages read but not translated,
and there are passages neither read nor translated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by bringing a ברייתא that organizes the משנה's topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three groups of passages: read and translated, read but not translated, and neither read nor translated.

steps.title: A memory code for the passages that are read and translated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts the first group and gives a memory code: בל"ת עק"ן נשפ"ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are read and translated. The memory code is: בל"ת עק"ן נשפ"ה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא gives a memory code whose letters each stand for one passage, and the גמרא will now decode it letter by letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter is the first letter of a passage in the 'read and translated' group. The code helped students remember the list in order. The decoding begins right away with ב for בראשית.

keyTerms.meaning: a memory code made of letters that stand for items in a list
the code letters; each letter stands for one passage

steps.confusionAlert: These three 'words' are not real words. They are just strings of first letters, so don't try to translate them.

phrases.english: These are read and translated:
Bet-Lamed-Tav, Ayin-Kuf-Nun, Nun-Shin-Peh-Heh is the mnemonic.
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for one passage, decoded below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ נִקְרִין וּמִתַּרְגְּמִין. בָּלַ״ת עָקָ״ן נִשְׁפֶּ״ה סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins filling in the first of the three groups named in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'read and translated' group is summarized by the code בל"ת עק"ן נשפ"ה.

steps.title: The Creation story is read and translated
steps.stepSummary: The first letter, ב, stands for מעשה בראשית, which is read and translated in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: The account of Creation is read and translated.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא decodes the first letter of the code. ב stands for בראשית, the story of Creation, and it may be read and translated publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts מעשה בראשית in the most permissive group. It may be read aloud and also translated, so everyone in the congregation understands it.

phrases.english: The account of Creation
is read and translated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decodes the first letter (ב) of the memory code.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשה בראשית is read and translated in public.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Why would anyone think the Creation story could not be read and translated? That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothered to say something that seems obvious. The Creation story is not embarrassing to anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other passages on these lists are sensitive because they are embarrassing or hidden. מעשה בראשית seems to have no such problem, so listing it looks pointless. The גמרא wants to know what possible concern this ruling rules out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it is obvious', a challenge asking why something needed to be said

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling just stated about מעשה בראשית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need to tell us that מעשה בראשית is read and translated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the Creation story is shameful or hidden, so of course it may be read and translated. Listing it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One might have feared forbidden questions about Creation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one might have thought public reading would lead people to ask what is above and what is below. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: people will come to ask what is above and what is below,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why the ruling is needed. One might have worried that reading Creation publicly would lead people to ask forbidden questions about what lies beyond the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not pointless. It rejects a real worry: that publicizing Creation would lead people into deep, forbidden speculation. The sentence is not finished here; the next passage will complete the reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'you might have said', which introduces the mistaken assumption a ruling comes to reject
'what is above, what is below', forbidden speculation about what lies beyond the world

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'מהו דתימא' introduces the wrong idea, the one the ברייתא is coming to reject. It is not the conclusion. The real conclusion is that מעשה בראשית is still read and translated.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
people will come to ask
what is above, what is below,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: אָתוּ לְשַׁיּוֹלֵי מָה לְמַעְלָה מָה לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by naming the worry the ruling comes to rule out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: identifies a plausible mistaken assumption that makes the ruling necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the ruling, one might think מעשה בראשית should not be read publicly, because it could lead people to ask what is above and what is below.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that it is still read and translated. The full reasoning is completed on the next amud.
